thread.title: Morning Movers: Facebook Sinks the Market Despite Trade Relief

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Morning Movers: Facebook Sinks the Market Despite Trade Relief
text:
By Teresa Rivas July 26, 2018 9:28 a.m. ET Unfriended. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is the only major index making headway this morning, as Facebook's hard plunge is weighing on the market. But that doesn't mean that investors shouldn't be relieved that the U.S. will apparently avoid a trade war with important ally, the European Union. In today's Morning Movers , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...parse what the U.S. gains from yesterday's agreement with the EU;
•...see why Facebook 's (FB) 20% fall is sinking the market;
•....check in on Altria 's (MO) earnings.
Oversharing
Stocks ended Wednesday on a high note on an agreement that may keep the U.S. from entering a trade war with Europe–a welcome, 11th-hour reversal from rhetoric earlier that day. However, stocks are poised to open lower on Thursday, as Facebook 's (FB) earnings weigh on tech.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 0.2% in early trading. However, the S&P 500 is 0.2% lower, and the Nasdaq Composite , which is of course even more tech heavy, is off 0.8%.
Despite the euphoria over yesterday's news, it's not surprising that the market is taking a hit following the Facebook report: After all, tech has grown to be the biggest component of the S&P 500 by a long shot, helping to pull the index up many times in the past, and earnings results have been strong enough to lift stocks out of tariff-related doldrums plenty of times this year.
Still, today's lower open doesn't negate the fact that the ceasefire between the U.S. and the EU is good news. Janney Montgomery Scott's Michael Gaugler writes that the "surprise twist" agreement to work toward "zero tariffs" has a twofold effect, allowing the U.S. avoid a trade war with a wealthy ally and helping it score a point over China. The news will not only "strengthen the U.S. and European Union economies, but pressure other economies toward 'zero tariff' agreements. China, in particular, looks to have lost significant leverage, as the Trump administration not only moved to protect farmers with $12 billion in direct aid , but obtained an agreement with the European Union to buy more soybeans, which we believe removes much of the leverage China was able to exert in trade/tariff discussions."
In addition, he writes that once the agreement with the Europeans is finalized, they will likely join the U.S in exerting pressure on Chin as well, which will further exacerbate that nation's "difficulties in maintaining the status quo with regards to tariffs and practices unfavorable to trading partners."
Speaking of difficulties, Facebook looks like it's in for a punishing day. The disappointment about its light second-quarter revenue wiped out all its year-to-date gains , and it got at least two downgrades, from Instinet and Raymond James , following its earnings report. And because the company and its fellow Faang stocks–a group that also includes Apple (AAPL), Amazon.com (AMZN), Netflix (NFLX) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL)–have such a heavy weighting in the S&P 500, it may be difficult for the index to make headway thanks to Facebook's malaise.
Talk about the wrong way to go viral.
Morning Movers
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is up 6.9% to $17.16 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The chip maker earned 14 cents a share on revenue of $1.76 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 12 cents a share on revenue of $1.72 billion.
Altria (MO) is down 4.1% to $55.50 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The tobacco giant earned $1.01 a share on revenue of $4.88 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1 a share on $5.02 billon. For the full year, it sees EPS of $3.94 to $4.03, compared with the $3.99 consensus estimate.
Celgene (CELG) is up 2% to$89.45 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The biotech earned $2.16 a share on revenue of $3.81 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $2.11 on revenue of $3.7 billion. For the full year, it sees EPS of $8.70 to $8.75, on revenue of $15 billion. Consensus calls for EPS of $8.52 on revenue of $14.91 billion.
Comcast (CMCSA) is up 4.6% to $34.87 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The cable giant earned 65 cents a share on revenue of $21.73 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 60 cents on revenue of $21.85 billion.
Facebook (FB) is down 20.7% to $172.53 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The social network earned $1.74 a share on revenue of $13.23 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of $1.70 on revenue of $13.35 billion. Daily active users rose 11% year-over-year.
Ford Motor (F) is down 3.6% to $10.14 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The auto maker earned 27 cents a share on revenue $35.9 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 30 cents on revenue of $35.63 billion.
Gilead Sciences (GILD) is down 2% to $77.35 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The biotech earned $1.91 a share on revenue of $5.65 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.56 a share on revenue of $5.2 billion. For the full year, it sees revenue of $20 billion to $21 billion, compared with the $20.8 billion consensus.
Las Vegas Sands (LVS) is down 2.8% to $73 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The casino operator earned 76 cents a share on revenue of $3.3 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 79 cents on revenue of $3.2 billion.
Mastercard (MA) is down 2.4% to $208.95 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The card giant earned $1.66 a share on revenue of $3.67 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of $1.53 on revenue of $3.65 billion.
Mattel (MAT) is down 7.6% to $15.05 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The toy maker lost 56 cents a share on revenue of $840.7 million. Analysts were looking for a loss of 30 cents a share on revenue of $862.48 million.
McDonald's (MCD) is down 0.6% to $158 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The fast-food behemoth earned $1.99 a share on revenue of $5.35 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of $1.92 on revenue of $5.32 billion.
Mondelez International (MDLZ) is up 3.6% to $43 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The packaged-food giant earned 56 cents a share on revenue of $6.11 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 54 cents on revenue of $6.12 billion.
PayPal Holdings (PYPL) is down 4.4% to $87.40 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The online-payments firm earned 58 cents a share on revenue of $3.86 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 56 cents on revenue of $3.81 billion. It also announced a $10 billion share-repurchase plan.
Qualcomm (QCOM) is up 6.4% to $63.25 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The chip firm earned $1.01 a share on revenue of $5.6 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 71 cents a share on revenue of $5.19 billion.
Under Armour (UAA) is up 9.7% to $23.12 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The athletic wear maker earned 8 cents a share on revenue of $1.7 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 8 cents on revenue of $1.15 billion.
Visa (V) is down 1.5% to $140.50 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The payments network firm earned $1.20 a share on revenue of $5.24 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.09 on revenue of $5.09 billion.
Upgrades & Downgrades
3D Systems (DDD) is down 5.1% to $13.29 after Piper Jaffray downgraded it to Underweight.
Cracker Barrel Old Country Store (CBRL) is up 0.6% to $164.23 after Maxim Group upgraded it to Buy.
e.l.f. Beauty (ELF) is down 1.8% to $13.83 after Oppenheimer downgraded it to Perform.
Skechers (SKX) is down 2.1% to $27.07 after Argus downgraded it to Hold.
